hints: Focus on how many sigma bonds plus lone pairs are around nitrogen, since that steric number tells you the hybridisation.
Draw the Lewis structure for each nitrogen and count: single bonds and pyramidal shapes usually mean sp3, while a triple bond means sp.
Look for the molecule where nitrogen makes only two electron domains in a straight line, one sigma bond to H via C plus a triple bond, to pick the sp case.
walkthrough:
**Recall the hybridisation rule**

Think of hybridisation as a code for shape. Count sigma bonds + lone pairs on the atom, this is the steric number.

Steric number 4 = $sp^3$, steric number 3 = $sp^2$, steric number 2 = $sp$

**Check the amines and acids first**

In $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ nitrogen has three single $\sigma$-bonds and one lone pair. That is 3 + 1 = 4, so $sp^3$.

In $\text{NH}_3$ nitrogen also has three $\sigma$-bonds and one lone pair. That is also 4, so $sp^3$ pyramidal.

**Check nitric acid**

In $\text{HNO}_3$, nitrogen is bonded to three oxygens with no lone pair on N. That is steric number 3, trigonal planar, so $sp^2$.

$$ \text{steric number} = 3 \; \sigma\text{-bonds} + 0 \; \text{lone pairs} = 3 \rightarrow sp^2 $$

**Spot the linear triple bond**

In $\text{H-C}\equiv\text{N}$, nitrogen has one $\sigma$-bond to carbon plus one lone pair. The other two bonds of the triple bond are $\pi$-bonds and do not count.

$$ \text{steric number} = 1 \; \sigma\text{-bond} + 1 \; \text{lone pair} = 2 \rightarrow sp $$
That linear, two-domain arrangement is the sp signature.

options.A: Incorrect. In $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ (ethylamine) nitrogen forms three single sigma bonds to C and two H atoms, plus one lone pair. Steric number 4 gives tetrahedral electron geometry and $sp^3$ hybridisation, not sp.
options.B: Incorrect. In $\text{HNO}_3$ nitrogen is bonded to three O atoms with one double bond and two single bonds in resonance, and has no lone pair. Steric number 3 gives trigonal planar geometry and $sp^2$ hybridisation.
options.C: Correct. In $\text{HCN}$, $\text{H-C}\equiv\text{N}$, nitrogen has only one sigma bond (to C) plus one lone pair, giving steric number 2 and linear geometry. This is exactly $sp$ hybridisation, with two sp orbitals and two unhybridised p orbitals forming the two pi bonds.
options.D: Incorrect. In $\text{NH}_3$ nitrogen has three N-H sigma bonds and one lone pair. Steric number 4 gives pyramidal shape and $sp^3$ hybridisation. Students sometimes confuse the presence of a lone pair with sp, but you must count all sigma bonds plus lone pairs.
